title: Orchestration & Dependency Injection
intro: Applies to: controllers, command/query handlers, console commands, event listeners, jobs, application services, middleware.

entries.rule: Application-layer classes **MUST** be orchestrators, not executors: resolve dependencies, delegate to a domain method, dispatch events/commands. Nothing else.
An orchestrator **MUST NOT**:
items: contain business logic (calculations, eligibility decisions, status derivation, interpreting vendor data vocabularies);
mutate model state directly (`$model->forceFill(...)->save()`, attribute assignment) instead of calling a domain method that owns the change;
create related records inline (looping over children calling `create()`) instead of one aggregate method;
call an external system (HTTP, filesystem, PDF, mail transport) directly instead of a dedicated infrastructure class.

entries.rule: Business logic **MUST** live in domain model methods (`Team::createPersonal()`, `$subscription->recordRenewal()`); infrastructure **MUST** live in dedicated service classes.

Guard clauses on coordination data (null payload, empty list), parsing inbound payloads into typed values, and routing an external event to the right domain method **MAY** stay in the orchestrator; that is coordination, not business logic.
entries.why: that is coordination, not business logic

entries.rule: Condition-plus-action **MUST** live on the model: `$sub->recoverIfPastDue()`, never `if ($sub->isPastDue()) { $sub->activate(); }` in a handler.

Lookups **MUST** use `findByXOrFail()` model methods, not `find()` plus a null check in the caller. A plain "find by id or 404" **MUST** use Eloquent's `findOrFail()`; a bespoke not-found exception **MUST NOT** be invented for a missing row. Custom exceptions are for genuine domain errors.

Comparisons **SHOULD** hide behind intention-revealing methods on the owning object (`$achievement->isEarnedAtLevel($level)`, `$a->isHigherThan($b)`), not raw attribute comparisons in an orchestrator. A primitive validity guard on a single scalar **MAY** stay inline.

sections.heading: Dependency injection: no facades, no helpers

entries.rule: Production classes **MUST NOT** use facades or global helpers. Inject contracts:
items: `Auth::` -> `Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\Factory` (controllers and middleware only; handlers never read the authenticated user, see "Controllers and handlers")
`app()`, `resolve()`, `collect()`: production classes **MUST NOT** call them. `app()` and `resolve()` are the Laravel form of the no-service-location rule in `php-core.md`.

entries.rule: Regular classes **MUST** use constructor injection; queued jobs **MUST** use method injection on `handle()`.

Facades and helpers **MAY** be used in: blade views, route files, migrations, service providers, factories, and tests. Filament pages and widgets have their own sanctioned `App::make(Dispatcher::class)` exception (see `filament.md`).
`declare(strict_types=1);` **MUST** open every PHP file. This family owns the file-shape rules for the whole codebase (models, migrations, factories, config, tests included).

Controllers, handlers, listeners, events, DTOs **MUST** be `final readonly class`. Queued jobs **MUST** be `final` but **MAY** drop `readonly` (queue interaction mutates state). The same applies to queued listeners that use `InteractsWithQueue`, whose untyped `$job` property a readonly class cannot hold.

Controllers **MUST NOT** extend the framework base `Controller` class; a single-action controller needs nothing from it, and PHP forbids a `readonly` class extending a non-readonly parent, so the extend itself blocks the shape rule. Import any needed concern explicitly instead.
entries.why: PHP forbids a `readonly` class extending a non-readonly parent

entries.rule: Constructor property promotion and explicit parameter/return types **MUST** be used. An empty constructor body **MUST NOT** exist; remove it.
Control structures **MUST** use curly braces, even single-line bodies.
Truthy/falsy checks (`if (! $x)`) **SHOULD** be preferred over explicit `=== null` comparisons, except where a falsy non-null value is legitimately distinct from null.
Comments **MUST NOT** narrate what the next line does and **MUST NOT** form step-by-step blocks. A brief why-comment (workaround, ordering constraint) or a short class-level PHPDoc **MAY** exist.
Controllers **MUST** be single-action (`__invoke()` only), never multi-action resource controllers.
A handler **MUST** expose exactly one public `handle(Command|Query): ReturnType`.
Handlers **MUST** return typed Result DTOs, never associative arrays.

A handler **MUST** receive the acting user as a parameter on its command; it **MUST NOT** read the authenticated user itself. Queued jobs and console commands have no logged-in user. The controller takes the actor from the authenticated principal, never from request input (see `authorization.md`).
entries.why: Queued jobs and console commands have no logged-in user

entries.rule: A controller **MUST NOT** call or inject another controller; shared work **MUST** move into a handler both call.
Controllers **MUST** return an API Resource or `JsonResponse` with an explicit status, never a bare array.
Controllers **MUST NOT** try/catch domain exceptions; domain exceptions render themselves (see `models-domain.md`).

Validation **MUST** live in Form Request classes with array-syntax rules (`['required', 'string']`), never inline `$request->validate([...])` and never string-pipe rules. Every Form Request **MUST** define both `authorize()` and `rules()`.

Domain events **MUST** be dispatched from the application layer. A model **MUST NOT** dispatch events and **MUST NOT** receive a `Dispatcher`; the model returns a value/decision, the orchestrator dispatches. Repeated decide-then-dispatch logic **SHOULD** be extracted into one small application-layer service.
Audit/history records **MUST NOT** be written inline in handlers, jobs, or model methods. Pattern: state change -> domain event -> a dedicated `final readonly` listener records it.

Mailables **MUST** implement `ShouldQueue` and **MUST** be sent from a listener via an injected `Mailer`, never the `Mail` facade and never inline from a command handler. Email is a side effect of a domain event.
Time-consuming or external work (HTTP calls, emails, heavy processing) **MUST** run in a `ShouldQueue` job, never synchronously in a handler or controller.

Every queued job/mailable **MUST** set its queue explicitly in the constructor via a backed `QueueName`-style enum (`$this->queue = QueueName::NOTIFICATIONS->value;`), never a raw string and never the implicit default.
Jobs that talk to external systems **MUST** declare explicit `$tries` and `$backoff`.

Queued jobs **MUST NOT** hold Eloquent models; they **MUST** carry ids or a small DTO with the values the job needs. Same rule as events (see `models-domain.md`): a serialized model goes stale and drags its loaded state into the queue payload.
entries.why: a serialized model goes stale and drags its loaded state into the queue payload

entries.rule: Query handlers **MUST** stay pure: no cache reads/writes inside a handler. Caching lives in a `Cached{Handler}` decorator wired in the service provider.
Cache keys, tags, and TTLs **MUST** come from centralized enum/key classes, never raw strings or hardcoded integers.
Cached payloads **MUST** stay user-agnostic: per-user data (access verdicts, ownership flags, personalization) resolves after the cache, in the controller, never baked into a shared cached entry.
Logging around a query handler **SHOULD** live in a decorator, like caching, not inside the handler. A handler **MAY** still log a domain decision only it knows.

Middleware aliases, groups and global middleware **MUST** be registered in `bootstrap/app.php` (`->withMiddleware(...)`), not in route files or an HTTP kernel. Route files only apply middleware by name (`->middleware('auth:sanctum')`).
